Yasemin Hoca is clearly very knowledgeable, and this was easy to feel throughout the course. Her lectures were very fluent, clear, and well-structured. Overall, I think Yasemin Hoca is a very strong and knowledgeable instructor, especially in the lecture part of the course. However, more consistent presence during critiques and clearer guidance about project expectations could make the term project process much easier and more productive for students.

The lecture part of the course was definitely very heavy. There was a large amount of information to learn, especially about ventilation systems, cooling, heating, and other technical topics. Because of this, preparing for the midterm was quite challenging.

However, I felt that the midterm did not fully reflect or support the heavy workload of the course. After studying and memorizing many different systems and concepts, we were given only three relatively limited questions. I would not say that the exam was easy, but the format did not seem to represent the amount of material we were expected to study.

One of the main difficulties was that we entered the midterm without a clear understanding of what kind of questions to expect. If we had solved a few practice exercises during the semester, or if sample questions had been provided, it would have been much easier to prepare. Instead, the assignments were mostly based on preparing a presentation and a poster. While these may be useful in some ways, they did not help me understand the exam expectations clearly.

I think this was one of the biggest issues with the course: students were expected to prepare for a heavy technical exam without enough guidance or practice beforehand. This made the midterm preparation process more stressful than it needed to be.

I also understand the purpose of having a term project, but managing it together with studio was difficult. Since studio already requires a lot of time and attention, balancing both courses at the same time became challenging. Overall, I think the course contains valuable information, but its workload, exam preparation process, and project expectations could be structured in a clearer and more manageable way.
